answer_1.quote: Grounded text generation, which includes tasks like summarization and question-answering, aims to produce content that is derived from specific sources...
answer_1.outputs: Summaries for MDS and responses for LFQA

answer_2.quote: Our evaluation methodology combines automated metrics and human judgments. Automatic Evaluation. To assess compliance with each task, we employ the ROUGE L and BERTSCORE metrics... For assessing citation conciseness, we report the average length (number of tokens) of the cited content per output sentence. To evaluate citation quality, we employ AUTOAIS... Lastly, we also report the average number of non-attributed sentences per instance.

answer_4.quote: For our human evaluation we used the Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) crowdsourcing platform... First, annotators are asked to evaluate text coherence on a 5-point Likert scale, and in the LFQA setting also its helpfulness in addressing the query. Next, annotators proceed to evaluate the quality of citations. We follow the sentence-level attribution evaluation protocol...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluate coherence on a 5-point Likert scale and (for LFQA) helpfulness; then judge attribution via the Attributable to Identified Sources (AIS) framework.
